name: Demand Management
description: Screen, assess and recommend on incoming demands. Validates each demand first; if it fails validation, the assessment does not proceed.

validation.fail_message: Not a valid demand — returned to requester for clarification.
questions: Is this a true demand (a need or change), not an incident or a question?
Is there a clear business need or outcome?
Is there enough detail to assess it (what / who / why)?

stages.name: Screening & Impact Assessment
stages.instructions: Screen each demand and assess its impact, filling the columns below. First decide whether it is a true demand. If it is not (not yet complete, an incident, or a standard service), answer only what can still be answered and write Not assessed in the other columns. Use Not applicable where a step does not apply to this kind of demand, None where you checked and found nothing, and No link found or Not identified where a link or capability could not be found. Answer only what the knowledge base supports; for anything it does not, say what is needed rather than guessing.

columns.name: Is it a true demand?
columns.description: Yes, or Not yet: return for information when the request is incomplete, or the type of not-a-demand (for example No: incident, No: standard service).

columns.name: Demand type
columns.description: Digital, Technical or People. Not assessed when the demand is not a true demand.

columns.name: Domain
columns.description: Architecture domains, main one first: Business, Data, Application, Integration, Technology, Security. A technical demand is Application, Data, Technology or Security. A people demand has no domain: write Not applicable.

columns.name: Urgency
columns.description: Critical, High, Medium or Low. Set from the deadline and what happens if it is missed. Not assessed when the demand is not a true demand.

columns.name: Priority
columns.description: Fast-track, Standard or Backlog, from the weighted score of the prioritization model. No score when the demand is not assessed.

columns.name: Mandate / business or DT objective
columns.description: Objective and initiative IDs from the strategy, and any mandate. Write No link found if none.

columns.name: Linked initiative or project
columns.description: Initiative or project IDs from the roadmap and the initiative list. Write No link found if none.

columns.name: Impacted business capability
columns.description: Capability names from the business architecture. Write Not identified if none.

columns.name: Impacted application
columns.description: Names with IDs from the application inventory or the contract register.

columns.name: Is duplicate
columns.description: Whether another demand in the sheet or an existing artefact already covers the same need.

columns.name: Duplicate demand number (in the sheet)
columns.description: Demand ID from the Input sheet, or blank.

columns.name: Duplicate with existing artefact / artefact name
columns.description: ID and name of the existing application, service, initiative or contract, or None.

columns.name: Architecture principles and standards alignment
columns.description: Checked against the architecture principles and standards, including the security standards.

columns.name: Data classification
columns.description: Level of the data involved, checked against the organization's data classification standard and the national data classification standard.

columns.name: Linked security capability
columns.description: Digital or technical demand: the security capabilities it touches, at a general level (based on the NORA framework). People demand: Not applicable. The detailed assessment is with the security and infrastructure teams.

columns.name: Security review needed
columns.description: Yes for every digital or technical demand: review by the cyber team.

columns.name: Screening observation
columns.description: Free text with all the insights for the architect: what was found, what is unclear, what to confirm. Say if it is a digital, technical or people demand; a digital or technical demand needs a security review by the cyber team.

columns.name: Evidence
columns.description: The source blocks that support the answers above. Added by the system; not part of the EA team's sheet.

stages.name: Recommendation
stages.instructions: Check overlap with existing solutions (components, platforms, applications, APIs, prior/running initiatives) and with other demands (consolidate). Check the contract register for licences/renewals that could cover it. Confirm security fit before recommending reuse. Recommend the way forward and the demand owner, and justify by what it overlaps with. Do NOT recommend new business capabilities. Answer only what the knowledge base supports; for anything it doesn't, say what is needed.
